title:
Every UI component implemented with React is represented by a type that ultimately mixes in this type.

In addition to being a marker type, it is responsible for producing a complete TSX file for use with the client.
This extra step allows us to keep the component itself DRY: fields declared on the type are automatically part of
its "props" without the need to declare a separate TypeScript type/interface and keep it in sync.

Data fields on the concrete component types (and its mixins) become available as the "props" of the component when
instantiated/rendered. Thus components should declare their props as part of their types. Primitive, collection and
reference types are all supported, but its best for the props to be relatively simple types, directly representable
in TypeScript.
